researcher_notes: Real project that is not yet a row of its own. Enable Mississippi River Transmission filed with the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission under docket CP26-2 for a 9.6 mile, 20 inch lateral from its Mainlines 2 and 3 at mile post 415.5 in Monroe County, Illinois to the Big Hollow Energy Center in Jefferson County, Missouri. The Energy Information Administration August 2026 pipeline projects workbook (Natural Gas Pipeline Projects sheet, Excel row 6) lists it as Approved, 200 MMcf/d added, in service 2028, and says the Missouri commission approved the Ameren project on 2/11/2026. Data center tie runs through the power plant. The lateral serves the Big Hollow Energy Center, an 800 megawatt Ameren Missouri gas plant. A St. Louis Public Radio story from October 31, 2025 says Ameren is building the plant in part for large load customers such as artificial intelligence data centers, and quotes Ameren's filing that building generation like Big Hollow is a critical part of serving them. No named campus, so the tie is medium specificity. A 2026 West Newsmagazine story reports Ameren signed confidential agreements with data centers, but it was not used as a ref. The two pages that name the lateral do not mention data centers. Not an existing row: Mississippi River Transmission (P0162) is the whole system with no segment for this lateral. The earlier name Ameren-EMRT Big Hollow Project is the EIA and filing name, so SegmentName follows it. Owner spelling comes from the filing; the ownership team's style tool found no close existing entity and no legal form beyond LLC. Capacity is the incremental figure. Route not researched, so RouteAccuracy is no route. Status is proposed: a federal certificate was reported as issued in June 2026 in the queue note but not verified here, and no construction start is set. Confidence medium.
